findings.text: Exposes a global descriptor for the cache type register under a human readable name, pairing its field table with an empty override holder for use by the feature framework.
Provides a globally visible helper that merges two observed values for one feature field into a conservative system wide value according to that field safety class.
Exposes mutable override holders for selected AArch64 memory model, processor feature, vector, streaming and instruction set registers and for software features, allowing boot time forcing of values.

Cache type fields are all strict except the I-cache policy field, with data cache maintenance, write granularity and line sizes using conservative merge rules and weakest policy reporting for mixed I-cache types to keep userspace just in time code correct.

Legacy memory model register zero fields stay hidden from userspace and use lower value wins merging, with shareability fields treated as signed and AuxReg allowed to vary across CPUs while others require uniformity.

AArch64 debug register zero fields stay hidden, with performance monitor version and profiling version allowed to differ across CPUs to support heterogeneous performance units while breakpoint, watchpoint and context comparator counts require uniformity and debug version uses exact match.

Vector floating point registers keep most fields hidden with lower wins merging, except double precision, fused multiply add, half precision and integer and load store fields which are visible to userspace but still strict and lower wins.

Cache zero and tag allocation granularity descriptors expose block size and prohibition flag to userspace with exact match for the prohibition flag and lower wins for size, while tag controller granularity stays hidden with lower wins.

Legacy instruction and memory model fields are generally hidden strict lower wins, with cryptographic, matrix multiply, brain float, speculation barrier, half precision multiply and dot product fields visible, and speculative SError reporting using higher wins on the reasoning that assuming an error is safer.

Legacy processor, debug and partitioning identifier fields stay mostly hidden strict lower wins, with speculative store bypass visible but allowed to vary, performance monitor exact, and partitioning limits allowing variation except for control register presence.
Fallback tables cover unlisted legacy registers as eight hidden strict lower wins nibbles, frequency as one hidden strict exact full word, and reserved zero registers as empty.

Registry pairs a numeric system identifier with a pointer to a register descriptor holding a name, a pointer to its field table and a pointer to its override holder plus computed consolidated value and masks for strict enforcement and userspace visibility.

Central table enumerates all known feature registers grouped by encoding, linking most to a shared empty override and selected AArch64 registers to dedicated mutable overrides, kept in strictly increasing identifier order to permit binary search.
Lookup uses a comparator that orders registry entries by numeric system identifier difference to support binary search.

Conservative merge returns the predefined safe value for exact fields, the smaller of the pair for lower safe fields, the larger for higher safe fields, and zero when either input is zero otherwise the larger for higher or zero safe fields.
Field insertion produces a register image with only the target bit range replaced by the supplied field value, preserving all other bits.

Boot initialization moves each field through override validation to one of four outcomes, applied when override is safe and different, redundant when equal, dropped with mask cleared when unsafe, or unrepresentable cleared, then folds the result into consolidated and userspace views.
Early boot validator checks that every field fits within sixty four bits, that fields within a register descend without overlap, and that registers ascend strictly, warning or aborting on violation.
Per register initializer builds consolidated system value and strict and user masks from the boot CPU reading constrained by overrides and safe defaults.
Capability index builder populates a direct lookup from capability number to descriptor from feature and errata tables, skipping out of range and duplicate entries with a warning.
Incorrect ordering of fields or registers breaks binary search and safe merging, so tables must respect descending field order without overlap and strictly increasing register order.
An unrecognized safety class triggers a fatal fault during safe value computation, so every field must use one of the four defined classes.
Cache type top bit is reserved one with safe one, I-cache policy weakest value corresponds to VIPT encoding, and data minimum line safe is one.
AArch64 debug architecture version safe is six and legacy shareability safe is fifteen, both encoding architectural baselines for conservative reporting.
Data cache zero prohibition flag safe is one, indicating prohibition by default for conservative userspace handling.
